2609.02339.title: AGI Maze Prediction Datasets: A Compact Benchmark for Learning World Dynamics with Transformers
2609.02339.paper_summary: World modeling requires a predictive model to maintain and update an internal state adequate for reasoning about the consequences of actions. We introduce the AGI Maze Prediction Datasets and Benchmark, a lightweight controlled testbed for studying this capability in Transformers and other predictive models. Derived from procedurally generated, stateful grid worlds, the benchmark comprises per-step transition prediction, fixed-horizon state prediction, and sequential textual-observation prediction. Source-maze-disjoint training and validation splits, together with greedy exact-match evaluation, distinguish learning transferable action-conditioned dynamics from memorizing transitions in familiar layouts. We establish from-scratch byte-level Transformer baselines and compare them with two working-memory-augmented architectures. A generic auxiliary latent-memory Transformer can fit some training sets perfectly but does not consistently improve held-out performance. In contrast, a pseudo-video spatial-memory Transformer initializes a two-dimensional latent workspace from the input map and updates it from action history without receiving intermediate maps, positions, or state labels. Under the same data, objectives, and evaluation protocol, this model reaches perfect validation accuracy on selected fixed-horizon tasks where the byte and unstructured-memory baselines do not, and substantially improves sequential text-trace prediction. These results suggest that structured, task-aligned working memory can be more useful than additional latent capacity alone. More broadly, we argue that language grounding is mediated by persistent data structures and computations over them; the benchmark offers a compact setting for testing architectures that couple textual interfaces to learned structured state.
2609.02339.paper_summary_zh: 世界建模需要一個預測模型來維持和更新內部狀態，以便對行動後果進行推理。<lb/>我們引入了AGI迷宮預測數據集和基準，這是一個輕量級的控制測試平台，用於研究Transformer和其他預測模型的這一能力。<lb/>該基準源自程序生成的有狀態網格世界，包含每步過渡預測、固定範圍狀態預測和序列文本觀察預測。<lb/>源迷宮不重疊的訓練和驗證拆分，以及貪婪的精確匹配評估，使得學習可轉移的行動條件動態與記憶熟悉佈局中的過渡區分開來。<lb/>我們建立了從零開始的字節級Transformer基準，並將其與兩種增強工作記憶的架構進行比較。<lb/>一個通用的輔助潛在記憶Transformer可以完美地擬合某些訓練集，但並未持續改善保留性能。<lb/>相比之下，一個偽視頻空間記憶Transformer從輸入地圖初始化一個二維潛在工作空間，並根據行動歷史進行更新，而不接收中間地圖、位置或狀態標籤。<lb/>在相同的數據、目標和評估協議下，該模型在選定的固定範圍任務上達到了完美的驗證準確率，而字節和非結構記憶基準則未能達到，並顯著改善了序列文本追蹤預測。<lb/>這些結果表明，結構化的、任務對齊的工作記憶可能比單純的額外潛在容量更有用。<lb/>更廣泛地說，我們認為語言的基礎是由持久數據結構及其上的計算所介導的；該基準提供了一個緊湊的環境，用於測試將文本接口與學習到的結構化狀態相結合的架構。
